record.title: LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics
record.summary: The LongChang preprint reports a benchmark for whether language models can notice unexpected behavior in simulated physical worlds, choose questions and test altered physical laws without assigned research tasks or hints. Across 12 models and 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, the authors report a 16.7% discovery rate for GPT-6-Astra and 0% for the other 11 models; discovery required both correct law identification and evidence support. In the ordinary-physics control, 36.1% of reports were rejected for false anomalies or unsupported explanations. GPT-6.1-Sol judged reports and GPT-6-Astra reviewed apparatus and generated/reviewed evolved scenes. These are author-reported results in a bounded simulation, not evidence of general scientific autonomy or real-world discovery.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors posted version 1 of the LongChang preprint to arXiv on October 27, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report evaluating 12 language models in 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, with three runs per model per scene and up to 100 turns per run, without a research task or hints about altered laws. GPT-6-Astra achieved a 16.7% discovery rate; the other 11 evaluated models scored 0%. Discovery required both correct identification of an altered law and experimental support in the exploration record.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the ordinary-physics control scene, the authors report that 36.1% of model reports were rejected for falsely claiming altered laws or giving unsupported explanations. The project page says each model was run three times per scene.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: GPT-6.1-Sol judged claim correctness and evidence support, while GPT-6-Astra reviewed apparatus and generated and reviewed evolved scenes. The paper therefore does not provide an evaluator-independent comparison of the evaluated models.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish autonomous discovery in physical laboratories or open-ended real science, performance beyond its simulated altered-physics tasks, or independent reproduction of its reported model comparisons.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of LongChang was inspected. The linked public repository currently contains a README and .github assets but states that source code is not included; its example benchmark commands require a configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint, API key, and model names.
The paper evaluates altered laws in MuJoCo simulations with explicit ground truth; it does not test open scientific domains whose correct explanations are not pre-specified.

brief.importance_rationale: If systems can notice unexpected behavior, form their own questions and design discriminating experiments, this could change how automated research capacity is evaluated. The reported result is confined to simulated physical-law discovery, so the score reflects potential importance rather than demonstrated real-world scientific capability.
limitations: All model-comparison results are author-reported preprint findings and have not been independently reproduced here.

The main comparison uses a normal-physics control plus 14 altered-law scenes in fixed-start MuJoCo simulations, with at most 100 turns; the findings do not establish transfer to laboratory experiments or open-ended science.
GPT-6.1-Sol judges correctness and evidence support, and GPT-6-Astra reviews apparatus and participates in scene generation/review, creating a model-role dependence in the evaluation pipeline.
GPT-6-Astra’s reported 16.7% discovery rate is distinct from its 97.6% evidence-support rate and 19.0% law-correctness rate; supported partial observations do not by themselves count as discovery.

The linked public repository README states that source code is not included; its benchmark run examples require an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, an API key, and configured explorer and judge models. No executable code or pinned model/API configuration was available in this inspection.

relationships.summary: LongChang reports free exploration in fixed-start MuJoCo simulations; the comparison study reports one nitrogen-vacancy spin experiment on human-assembled apparatus with preset safety limits. These distinct regimes bound the evidence: the simulated benchmark does not establish physical-laboratory autonomy.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that one of 12 evaluated models achieved nonzero evidence-supported altered-law discovery under free exploration in a bounded MuJoCo simulation benchmark.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint’s publication and reported experimental protocol are directly inspectable. The experimental outcomes remain claims by the authors and were not reproduced in this activation.
technical.mechanism: Explorers receive observations and physical actions in simulated scenes, choose what to investigate, may design apparatus, and record action rationales and observations. A separate LLM judge checks reports against hidden altered laws and complete exploration records for correctness and evidence support. Exploration records guide separate LLM scene designers/reviewers in evolving later scenes.
technical.regime: 12 language models; 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes comprising a normal-physics control and 14 scenes with one altered physical law; up to 100 turns per main evaluation. GPT-6.1-Sol judges reports; GPT-6-Astra reviews apparatus and generates/reviews evolved scenes.
technical.reproducibility: The author project page reports three runs per model per scene. The linked public repository README says source code is not included and its run examples require an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, API key, explorer model and judge model. No executable source, pinned benchmark manifest, independent run or evaluator-independent score audit was available in this inspection.
technical.strongest_baseline: The benchmark compares 12 models under shared scene and turn conditions, with three runs per model per scene; it includes a normal-physics false-discovery control and reports controlled conditions for task guidance, turn budget and apparatus access. The paper uses GPT-6.1-Sol as judge and GPT-6-Astra for apparatus and scene-generation/review roles. The linked repository does not currently expose executable source code, and there is no independent reproduction.

brief.title: LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics
brief.why_it_matters: LongChang turns free-form scientific inquiry into a testable benchmark: a system must notice an anomaly, choose a question, devise experiments, and support its conclusion from an exploration record. The reported low discovery rate and normal-control false-discovery rejections show both the promise and difficulty of this narrow task. The simulation and evaluator/model-role limits mean the result does not establish autonomous discovery in physical laboratories or open-ended research.

other.title: A collaborative AI laboratory reports a theory-led diamond-spin experiment
other.summary: A preprint reports a collaborative LLM-agent laboratory that derived and tested a calibration law for ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond. The agents rejected an initial design because ordinary interpolation could make the same predictions, then classified an acquisition as inconclusive when phase and reference controls failed during signal drift. Authors report that agents revised the protocol without relaxing precommitted criteria; a six-hour randomized acquisition then passed the stated controls and supported predictions on four withheld pulse sequences. These are author-reported results from one laboratory study. The public Auctopus repository’s README says its mock-model offline demo does not reproduce the paper and that study prompts are not included; experimental data and analysis are available from the corresponding author on request.
